questions.scenario: Which AWS service provides access to foundation models through an API without managing infrastructure?
questions.explain: Bedrock provides serverless API access to foundation models from multiple providers. SageMaker AI is for building and training your own models, which requires far more expertise and management.

questions.scenario: A startup with no data scientists wants to build an application using an existing foundation model and manage no infrastructure. Which service?
options: Train a custom model on Amazon SageMaker
Self-host a model on Amazon EC2
questions.explain: No data scientists, no infrastructure, and using an existing foundation model all describe Bedrock. SageMaker and EC2 self-hosting require exactly the expertise they lack, and Lex builds intent-based chatbots rather than general content generation.

questions.scenario: Which service extracts text and data from scanned documents and forms?
questions.explain: Textract extracts text, forms and tables from scanned documents — 'text' plus 'extract'. Comprehend analyses meaning in text that already exists, and Rekognition analyses images and video.

questions.scenario: Which service converts recorded speech into written text?
questions.explain: Transcribe converts speech to text; Polly does the reverse, generating speech from text. Remember Polly as the parrot that speaks.

questions.scenario: Which AWS feature implements Retrieval Augmented Generation without building the retrieval pipeline yourself?
questions.explain: Knowledge Bases is AWS's managed RAG implementation, handling chunking, embedding and retrieval. Guardrails handles safety, Clarify handles bias, and Prompt Management stores and versions prompts.

questions.scenario: Which storage option is commonly used to hold embeddings for a RAG application on AWS?
questions.explain: OpenSearch Service is a vector store for embeddings, as are Aurora, Neptune and RDS for PostgreSQL. Glacier is archival storage, CloudTrail is auditing, and Polly generates speech.

questions.scenario: Which term describes a model that performs excellently on training data but poorly on new, unseen data?
questions.explain: Overfitting means the model memorised the training data rather than learning generalisable patterns. Underfitting means it learned too little and performs poorly everywhere.

questions.scenario: Which AWS service provides documentation about a model's intended use, training data and limitations?
questions.explain: Model Cards document a model's purpose, data and limitations, supporting transparency. Clarify explains why decisions were made (explainability) — a related but distinct concept.

questions.scenario: Which service discovers personally identifiable information stored in Amazon S3?
questions.explain: Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data such as PII in S3. GuardDuty detects threats, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, and Artifact provides compliance reports.

questions.scenario: Which service records who called which API and when, providing an audit trail for AI workloads?
questions.explain: CloudTrail is the audit trail of API activity, answering 'who did what'. CloudWatch monitors performance metrics, and Config tracks resource configuration state.

questions.scenario: What is a token in the context of large language models?
options: A small piece of text, roughly three-quarters of a word
questions.explain: Tokens are the chunks of text models read and generate, roughly three-quarters of a word each, and they are the unit you are billed on. The security meaning of 'token' is unrelated here.

questions.scenario: Which of these is a widely cited DISADVANTAGE of generative AI?
options: It can produce confident but factually incorrect output
questions.explain: Hallucination — confident but false output — is generative AI's best-known weakness, alongside limited interpretability and nondeterminism. The other options are simply untrue of GenAI.

questions.scenario: Which prompting technique provides several worked examples inside the prompt to guide the model?
questions.explain: Few-shot prompting includes several examples, improving consistency and format adherence. Zero-shot provides none, one-shot provides exactly one, and chain-of-thought asks for step-by-step reasoning.

questions.scenario: A company wants to reduce inference cost while keeping most of a large model's quality. Which technique applies?
questions.explain: Distillation produces a smaller, cheaper model that approximates a larger one's behaviour, directly reducing inference cost. More examples and a bigger context window increase token usage and therefore cost.

questions.scenario: Which of these is an appropriate use case for traditional machine learning rather than generative AI?
options: Predicting next month's product demand from historical sales
questions.explain: Forecasting a numeric value from historical data is traditional ML (regression). Writing, image generation and summarisation all create new content, which is generative AI's domain.

questions.scenario: Which service inserts human review into an AI workflow for low-confidence or high-risk predictions?
questions.explain: A2I builds human review into workflows, routing uncertain or sensitive predictions to people. Clarify measures bias and explainability, and Guardrails filters content.

questions.scenario: Which TWO AWS services help demonstrate regulatory compliance for AI workloads?
questions.explain: Artifact supplies AWS's compliance reports and Audit Manager collects evidence for your own audits. Polly, Rekognition and Lex are AI capabilities with no compliance-reporting function.

questions.scenario: Which factor should be considered when selecting a foundation model for a latency-sensitive application?
options: The colour of the console interface
The number of AWS Regions in total
questions.explain: Model size, latency, modality, cost, customisability and input/output length are the selection criteria named by the exam guide. Larger models are generally slower, which matters for latency-sensitive use.

questions.scenario: What does 'multi-modal' mean when describing a foundation model?
options: It can process more than one type of data, such as text and images
It runs in multiple AWS Regions
It supports multiple users at once
questions.explain: Multi-modal means handling several data types — commonly text plus images. Modality refers to the kind of data, not deployment or pricing.

questions.scenario: Which metric measures, of all the genuinely positive cases, how many the model correctly identified?
questions.explain: Recall measures how many true positives were caught, so it matters when missing a case is costly — disease screening or fraud detection. Precision measures how many flagged cases were genuine.
